_readme: The automatic join is deliberately conservative: when several real people
share a surname and first initial it refuses to guess, which is correct but
left out many of the biggest names in T20 cricket (Rohit Sharma, Bumrah,
Rashid Khan, Dwayne Bravo, Steve Smith). Each entry below was checked
individually against at least three independent signals -- the expansion of
the Cricsheet initials, country, franchise history, career span, and the
statistical profile (wickets/economy/strike rate) -- and the `why` field
records that evidence so any entry can be re-audited later.
This is a human identity assertion, NOT invented data: it only says WHICH
existing SportMonks record belongs to WHICH existing Cricsheet player. No
stat, style, or nationality is authored here.
Overrides are applied before every automatic pass and are still held to the
one-to-one rule -- reconcile.mjs fails loudly if two of them claim the same
SportMonks id, or if an id does not exist in the directory.

overrides.why: RG = Rohit Gurunath. India + Deccan Chargers (2008-10) then Mumbai Indians matches his real club history; 434 matches 2007-2026; 16 wickets of occasional offbreak matches SportMonks' right-arm-offbreak.

JJ = Jasprit Jasbirsingh. Mumbai Indians + India only, IPL debut 2013 matches firstYear 2013; 308 wickets at 7.09 is a frontline quick, matching right-arm-fast. Decoy was Jagdeep Bumrah (id 58320), also India, which is why the auto-join abstained.

Afghanistan, dob 1998, legbreak-googly. 411 wickets at 6.79 economy from 2016 is the leading T20 legspinner; Adelaide Strikers / Sunrisers Hyderabad / Gujarat Titans is his exact franchise record. Four other Khans contested this key.
DJ = Dwayne John. 539 wickets, the most in T20 history, at fast-medium; 2006-2024 and CSK/Melbourne Renegades. Distinct from his cousin Darren (DM) Bravo, id 124.

SA = Suryakumar Ashok. KKR (2014-17) then Mumbai Indians then India is his exact path; average 34.7 at strike rate 154 is his signature profile. Contested by Kuldeep and Umesh Yadav on the same surname.
SPD = Steven Peter Devereux. Australia; Rising Pune Supergiant + Rajasthan Royals + Sydney Sixers; 27 wickets of legbreak-googly matches SportMonks' listed style.
AJ = Aaron James. Australia; Melbourne Renegades plus the unusually long IPL list (Gujarat Lions, Kings XI, RCB, KKR) is his real record; 7 wickets of part-time slow left-arm.
KD = Krishnakumar Dinesh; universally known by his middle name. India wicketkeeper, zero wickets across 315 matches; Gujarat Lions/KKR/RCB/Delhi matches his club history.
MM = Moeen Munir. England allrounder, left-hand-bat, 220 wickets of offbreak at 7.64 economy; RCB and CSK spells match.
India; Pune Warriors then Sunrisers Hyderabad then RCB is an exact and distinctive franchise sequence; 311 wickets fast-medium from 2011.
AR = Akshar Rajeshbhai. Kings XI Punjab then Delhi Capitals then India; 235 wickets of slow left-arm orthodox and left-hand-bat both match. Decoy was Ajaz Patel (NZ), who never played those teams.
SL = Separamadu Lasith. Sri Lanka, right-arm-fast; Mumbai Indians; 304 wickets; career ends 2020, the year he retired.
Pakistan allrounder, right-arm-offbreak; 103 wickets across 2006-2025, one of the longest careers in the data, matching dob 1982.

dob 1980 Pakistan allrounder, legbreak: 255 wickets at 6.83 with a 153.6 strike rate is unmistakably Boom Boom, 2006-2022. NOTE the directory holds a SECOND, younger Shahid Afridi (id 15093, dob 1997) -- that name collision is exactly why the auto-join abstained.
Pakistan left-arm-fast-medium, dob 2000; career starts 2018 and 305 wickets; Lahore Qalandars is his home franchise. Distinct from Shahid Afridi above.
PWH de Silva is Wanindu Hasaranga de Silva -- SportMonks files him under Hasaranga, so no surname key could ever have matched. Sri Lanka legbreak, 279 wickets from 2017, RCB and Rajasthan Royals.
India, left-hand-bat, slow left-arm orthodox with 61 wickets; 2007-2019 and the Kings XI/Pune/RCB/SRH/MI sequence match his real career.
India left-hand-bat opener; KKR and Delhi Daredevils only; zero wickets in 188 matches; 2007-2018 matches his retirement.
India left-arm wrist spin (chinaman); KKR then Delhi Capitals then India; career from 2016.
LRPL = Luteru Ross Poutoa Lote. New Zealand middle-order; 2006-2025; Caribbean franchise spells (Jamaica Tallawahs, Guyana) match.
DPMD = Denagamage Praboth Mahela de Silva. Sri Lanka; 2006-2017 matches his retirement year; distinct from Sineth Jayawardene (born 2004).
NLTC = Narangoda Liyanaarachchilage Thisara Chirantha. Sri Lanka bowling allrounder, left-hand-bat, fast-medium; 2010-2025.
India left-arm-fast-medium, dob 1999; Kings XI Punjab -> Punjab Kings -> India, career from 2019. Distinct from Arshdeep Singh Brar (id 8157, offbreak, dob 1993).
Pakistan wicketkeeper, dob 1987; Quetta Gladiators is the franchise he captained.
MD = Mudiyanselage Dasun. Sri Lanka fast-medium allrounder; Bangladesh Premier League spells match.
BKG = Balapuwaduge Kusal Gimhan. Sri Lanka; Gujarat Titans and Sri Lankan franchise sides match.
DR = Dwayne Romel. West Indies, dob 1983, right-arm-fast-medium; Bangladesh franchise sides match. Distinct from Steven (SPD) and Devon (DS) Smith.
West Indies wicketkeeper-batter, dob 1989; Bangladesh Premier League sides (Rangpur, Rajshahi, Sylhet) match.
India legbreak; Delhi Daredevils -> Delhi Capitals -> Lucknow Super Giants is his exact club sequence.
UT = Umeshkumar Tilak. India right-arm-fast; KKR, RCB and Gujarat Titans match his club history.
JA = Johannes Albertus; known as Albie. South Africa fast-medium allrounder; Chennai Super Kings and St Lucia match. Distinct from his brother Morne.
CH = Christopher Henry. South Africa fast-medium; Delhi Daredevils/Capitals and Sydney Thunder match.
SR = Samit Rohit. England slow left-arm orthodox allrounder; Melbourne Renegades and Bangladesh franchise spells match.
